answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity proofs to a verified hardware enclave, funneling validation through an on-chain jetty gateway. Each agent deposits staked collateral into a smart vault and proves valid computation via zero-knowledge proofs coupled with cryptographic attestation chains. As a Sybil swarm multiplies, sequential registration incurs exponential capital exhaustion, making massive replication economically infeasible. Like forging unbreakable ferrous armor around the network, the superlinear cost model guarantees attacker insolvency.
